newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia arrests foreigners for drug smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia arrests foreigners for drug smuggling.

text.p: The Saudi authorities have arrested three foreigners apparently posing as Moslem pilgrims on charges of drug smuggling, a Saudi newspaper reported on Saturday.
The alleged traffickers -- two men and a woman -- were apprehended at Jeddah airport on Friday, al-Riyadh newspaper quoted a customs official as saying.
It said they entered Saudi Arabia on visas for visitors performing the Umra, a minor pilgrimage which can take place at any time of the year and takes just over an hour to complete.
The newspaper did not give their names.
It said the woman, carrying 42 grams of cocaine in "a sensitive part", was from an unidentified West African country.
One of the men, from an unnamed Asian country, was hiding 358 grams of heroin "inside him", the newspaper said.
The second man was carrying 678 grams of heroin.

Convicted drug smugglers and dealers face public beheading by the sword in Saudi Arabia. In 1995, the conservative Islamic kingdom executed 192 people, mostly convicted drug smugglers from the Indian sub-continent.
